service_org_legal_entity.quote: SOC 2 Report for CEREBRAS SYSTEMS INC. A Type 2 Independent Service Auditor's Report on Controls Relevant to Security and Confidentiality
service_org_legal_entity.note: Rendered in all caps with NO comma before 'INC.' throughout (cover, assertion, auditor's report). System name: 'Cerebras AI Inference Cloud'. Narrative also says 'Cerebras Systems Inc. ("Cerebras") is a private technology company headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.' (p10).

auditor_firm.note: Signature block at end of Independent Service Auditor's Report (Section 2); also 'Prescient Assurance LLC conducted the examination testing throughout the period December 01, 2024, to November 30, 2025' (p26).

report_period.quote: A Type 2 Independent Service Auditor's Report on Controls Relevant to Security and Confidentiality December 1, 2024 To November 30, 2025

soc2_type.quote: SOC 2 Report for CEREBRAS SYSTEMS INC. A Type 2 Independent Service Auditor's Report

trust_services_criteria.quote: trust services criteria relevant to Security and Confidentiality set forth in TSP section 100

3.1.1.quote: Cerebras enforces Transport Layer Security (TLS) version 1.2 or above, which includes encryption to provide a secure browser session for individuals accessing Cerebras' public website.

supporting_quotes.quote: Encryption methods utilized for data in-transit include (but are not limited to) Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 or later, Secure Shell (SSH) 2.0 or later
API requests and responses are transmitted over HTTPS, using TLS to prevent unauthorized parties from intercepting data.

3.1.1.notes: Report states 'TLS 1.2 or later/or above' — TLS 1.2 is the named minimum; TLS 1.3 is not explicitly named.

3.1.2.quote: Cerebras uses cryptographic controls to protect the confidentiality of sensitive data when the data is in transit or at rest. Customer data is encrypted in storage and during transmission over external networks.

supporting_quotes.quote: In-scope data is encrypted at rest. Inspected the AWS S3 bucket encryption status report to determine that in-scope data is encrypted at rest.
Encryption algorithms used by Cerebras are based on industry best practices and standards.

3.1.2.notes: Encryption at rest is attested (auditor-tested against AWS S3 bucket encryption status) but the report never names an algorithm (no AES-128/192/256 anywhere), so no exact dropdown match.

3.1.4.quote: Cryptographic keys used in the production environment are securely stored and are rotated on a periodic basis.

supporting_quotes.quote: platform secrets, such as certificates and keys used for internal communication, are restricted to authorized Cerebras personnel.

3.1.4.notes: Keys are Cerebras production-environment keys held and rotated by Cerebras; no customer-managed or customer-specific key option is described. Who 'generates' keys is not explicitly worded — flag for reviewer.

3.1.8.value:
Phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication (MFA) required to connect to the production environment
Endpoint hard-drive encryption enforced; EDR deployed on servers and workstations
VPN encryption for communications into and out of data centers; remote sessions encrypted
Periodic rotation of production cryptographic keys; platform secrets restricted to authorized personnel
Internal and external vulnerability scans on a regular basis plus independent penetration testing
Quarterly user access reviews; secure media disposal per Data Security Policy
3.1.8.quote: Furthermore, phishing-resistant multifactor authentication (MFA) is required to connect to the production environment

3.2.1.quote: Cerebras Systems Inc. ("Cerebras") is a private technology company headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.
3.2.1.notes: The report names no hosting regions and makes no EU/data-residency statement. Subservice organizations (carve-out, pp21-24): Cloudflare (web application services), Amazon Web Services (cloud infrastructure), and colocation data centers — Colovore, Nautilus Data Technologies, Tierpoint, LLC, Legacy/T5 Data Centers, Scale Data Centers, Enovum Data Centers; their facility locations are not disclosed in the report.

absent: 3.1.3 backup encryption — the report contains no backup/restore control for customer data at all (the only 'backup' mentions are boilerplate criteria text, e.g. 'back-up media storage' in CC6.4, pp65-66); user entities are told to develop their own disaster recovery plans (p21).
3.1.6 anonymization — the words 'anonymize/anonymized' do not appear in the report.
3.1.7 pseudonymization — the word 'pseudonym' does not appear in the report.
At-rest algorithm — 'encrypted at rest' attested but no AES/algorithm named (relevant to 3.1.2); algorithms only described as 'based on industry best practices and standards' (p18).
Hosting locations / EU statements — no regions or countries stated for production infrastructure or the colocation data centers (relevant to 3.2.1/3.2.2).
Customer-specific vs shared key statement (relevant to 3.1.4).
